post.title: Fake class action settlement texts: the FTC red flags
post.ig:
Imposters took a reported $3.5 billion in 2025, per the FTC, and fake settlement notices are one disguise.

Imposter scam losses reported to the FTC rose from about $1.2B in 2020 to $3.5B in 2025.
In September 2026 the FTC raised Amazon Prime refunds to up to $200, and says: "No one from the FTC or Amazon will ask you for money to get a refund."
BBB red flags (2026): upfront fees, requests for SSN or bank info, vague case details, pressure to act now.
Real class actions are approved by a judge, and the claims administrator is paid from the settlement. A 2019 FTC staff study found a median claims rate of just 9%.

Sources: FTC Consumer Sentinel 2025 data (June 2026); FTC Amazon refunds page and press release (Sept 2026); BBB warnings (2026); FTC staff report Consumers and Class Actions (Sept 2019).
News and education, not financial advice.
